newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Western Australia says has petrochem interest.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Western Australia says has petrochem interest.

text.p: At least five overseas companies, including Dow Chemical Co and Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, have expressed interest in participating in a Western Australia petrochemical project, state resources and energy minister Colin Barnett said on Friday.
Barnett said in a radio interview the government would soon be inviting formal expressions of interest from the groups as well as companies in South Korea and Germany.
He said he expected a petrochemical plant to be operating in the Pilbara region of the north west of the state by 2000-2001.
"This is a real project (with) great international interest and we will manage it well," Barnett said.
"I am confident we will see this development," he said.
"In our last term of government our number one development objective was the Gas-to-the-Goldfields project," Barnett said.

"Petrochemicals in the Pilbara is the target this time," he said. "Because there is only enough gas to support one (plant)at this stage the government is about to start a competitive open process," he said. "We'll invite expressions of interest, submissions from all of these major groups." he said.
"This something the government has been working on quietly for the last year with gas producers and potential investors."

Barnett said Western Australia was in the fortunate position of having a number of big projects reaching the "go-ahead" stage, including a steel mill planned by Kingstream Resources NL and Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co Ltd.

"Kingstream is progressing well. In fact, in the next two weeks I will be visiting Taiwan to try and conclude negotiations on that project and we expect to have a state agreement brought into Parliament when it resumes next month," Barnett said.
"I think the real crunch time for that project will be around mid-year when they (the Kingstream consortium) would hope to conclude their financing arrangements," Barnett said.
"In fact, there are about three or four major iron ore projects at different stages of development," he said.
"But we are not going through a boom-bust cycle," he said.
"This state is going through a sustained period of development that has not been seen in our history and, I dare say, Australian history," the minister said.
